core_obligations: Observe that the given morphism Y' to Y can be regarded as a family of morphisms forming a tau covering (proof lines 5564-5565).
Apply the locality of P on the target to conclude that the base change of f along that morphism has P (proof lines 5563-5565).
proof_roadmap: Fit the morphism into a covering family (proof lines 5564-5565).
Transfer the property by locality on the target.
difficulty_reason: For a topology tau among fpqc, fppf, syntomic, smooth, etale and Zariski, a property P of morphisms which is tau local on the target, and a morphism f with P, the lemma shows that the base change of f along any morphism which is flat, flat and locally of finite presentation, syntomic, etale or an open immersion again has P (statement lines 5552-5560). The proof names the reason in one step: the given morphism can be fitted into a family of morphisms forming a tau covering, and then the locality of P on the target transfers the property to the base change (proof lines 5563-5565). The claim is H2: the argument is short, but it identifies exactly which covering family is being used and why the single base change morphism is legitimate input for the locality axiom, which the five listed cases share.
